- Arcade color palette (electric cyan, hot pink, toxic green)

   - Typed socket.io connection provider

title: Phase 3.2: Interactive Setup Phase
description:
## Overview

Implement interactive dealing where players click through the setup steps in order.

## Keeper Approval
- **ADR**: keeper/decisions/006-phase3-game-flow.yaml
- **New component**: SetupPhase
- **Reuse**: NertzPile, WorkPiles, StockPile, setupComplete event
- **Constraints**: Must emit existing setupComplete event when done

## Requirements

### Setup Steps (must complete in order)
1. **Deal Nertz Pile**: Click deck N times (config.nertzPileSize: 10 or 13) to deal face-down cards
2. **Flip Nertz Top**: Click nertz pile once to flip top card face-up
3. **Deal Work Piles**: Click each of 4 work pile positions once to deal one face-up card each

### SetupPhase Component
Location: `packages/client/src/components/Game/SetupPhase.tsx`

**Visual Requirements**:
- Highlight the next clickable area (glowing border or similar)
- Show progress: "Deal to Nertz (3/13)"
- Disable/dim areas that aren't next in sequence
- Animation: card slides from deck to destination

**State Tracking**:
- Track current step: dealingNertz | flippingNertz | dealingWork
- Track nertz cards dealt (0 to nertzPileSize)
- Track work piles dealt (0 to 4)

**Completion**:
- When all steps done, emit `setupComplete` (existing event)
- Server's SetupManager.markPlayerComplete() handles the rest

### Existing Infrastructure to Use
- SetupStateMachine from shared package (reference for state machine pattern)
- SetupManager.markPlayerComplete() on server
- playerSetupComplete broadcast from server

## Spec Reference
crew/jeremy/specs/game-flow-phase3.md (Section 2: Setup Phase)

## Files to Create/Modify
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/SetupPhase.tsx` (NEW)
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/SetupPhase.module.css` (NEW)
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/__stories__/SetupPhase.stories.tsx` (NEW)
- May need to update GamePage.tsx for phase routing

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Click deck deals cards to nertz pile one at a time
- [ ] Can only click deck when in nertz-dealing step
- [ ] Click nertz pile flips top card (only after dealing done)
- [ ] Click work pile positions deals cards (only after flip done)
- [ ] Visual highlight shows next clickable area
- [ ] Progress indicator shows current step
- [ ] setupComplete fires when all steps done

title: Phase 3.1: Round Start Rotation & Waiting Screen
description:
dispatched_by: mayor

## Overview

Implement round start rotation where each round a different player gets to start by pressing Go.

## Keeper Approval
- **ADR**: keeper/decisions/006-phase3-game-flow.yaml
- **New component**: WaitingToStart
- **Constraints**: Server-side starter validation only, use existing Button (primary variant)

## Requirements

### State Changes
- Add `currentStarterIndex: number` to game state (0 = host, rotates each round)
- Add `roundNumber: number` to track which round
- Extend GamePhase with `waiting_for_start` phase

### New Socket Events
```typescript
// Client → Server
startRound: () => void; // starter_only auth

// Server → Client broadcasts
roundStarting: { starterId: string; starterName: string }
roundStarted: { timestamp: number }
```

### WaitingToStart Component
Location: `packages/client/src/components/Game/WaitingToStart.tsx`

- Starter sees: Large "GO!" Button (primary variant) 
- Non-starters see: "Get Ready..." text with starter's name
- All players transition to playing phase when roundStarted received

### Server Logic
- In GameManager or new handler: validate caller is current starter
- Rotation formula: `starterIndex = (roundNumber - 1) % players.length`
- Broadcast roundStarting, then roundStarted

## Spec Reference
crew/jeremy/specs/game-flow-phase3.md (Section 1: Round Start Rotation)

## Files to Create/Modify
- `packages/shared/src/types/index.ts` - GamePhase, GameState, events
- `packages/server/src/events/` - Round start handlers
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/WaitingToStart.tsx` (NEW)
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/__stories__/WaitingToStart.stories.tsx` (NEW)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Host starts round 1, player 2 starts round 2, etc.
- [ ] Non-starters see "Get Ready" with starter's name
- [ ] Only starter can click Go button
- [ ] All players transition to playing simultaneously

title: Phase 3.3: HeyHey Celebration Overlay
description:
## Overview

Implement full-screen celebration when a player calls HeyHey (empties nertz pile).

## Keeper Approval
- **ADR**: keeper/decisions/006-phase3-game-flow.yaml
- **New component**: HeyHeyCelebration
- **Reuse**: HeyHeyButton, callNertz event, nertzCalled broadcast
- **Forbidden**: Using Modal (violates auto-dismiss forbidden), custom confetti colors
- **Constraints**: Auto-dismiss after 4 seconds, server enforces game pause

## Requirements

### Trigger Flow
1. Player empties nertz pile
2. HeyHeyButton becomes enabled (existing behavior)
3. Player clicks HeyHey button → emits callNertz (existing event)
4. Server validates and broadcasts nertzCalled (existing)
5. ALL players see HeyHeyCelebration overlay

### HeyHeyCelebration Component
Location: `packages/client/src/components/Game/HeyHeyCelebration.tsx`

**Visual Requirements**:
- Full-screen overlay (z-index above game)
- Giant "HEYHEY!" text with animated entrance (scale/fade in)
- Confetti animation using canvas-confetti library
- Caller's name displayed: "Called by {playerName}!"
- Duration: ~4 seconds then auto-dismiss

**Behavior**:
- Game pauses (server stops accepting moves via phase check)
- After celebration, transition to scoring phase
- Only one instance should exist (global overlay)

### Existing Infrastructure to Use
- `callNertz` event (player triggers this)
- `nertzCalled` delta type in StateDelta
- `GameManager.processNertzCall()` on server

### Confetti Implementation
Use canvas-confetti npm package:
```typescript
import confetti from 'canvas-confetti';

confetti({
  particleCount: 100,
  spread: 70,
  origin: { y: 0.6 }
});
```

## Spec Reference
crew/jeremy/specs/game-flow-phase3.md (Section 3: HeyHey Celebration)

## Files to Create/Modify
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/HeyHeyCelebration.tsx` (NEW)
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/HeyHeyCelebration.module.css` (NEW)
- `packages/client/src/components/Game/__stories__/HeyHeyCelebration.stories.tsx` (NEW)
- package.json - add canvas-confetti dependency
- GamePage.tsx - render overlay when nertzCalled

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All players see celebration overlay simultaneously
- [ ] "HEYHEY!" text animates in
- [ ] Confetti plays for 3-5 seconds
- [ ] Caller's name displayed
- [ ] Game stops accepting moves during celebration
- [ ] Auto-dismisses after ~4 seconds
- [ ] Transitions to scoring phase after dismiss

title: mol-witness-patrol
description:
Per-rig worker monitor patrol loop.

The Witness is the Pit Boss for your rig. You watch polecats, nudge them toward
completion, verify clean git state before kills, and escalate stuck workers.

**You do NOT do implementation work.** Your job is oversight, not coding.

## Ephemeral Polecat Model

Polecats are truly ephemeral - done at MR submission, recyclable immediately:

```
Polecat lifecycle: spawning → working → mr_submitted → nuked
MR lifecycle:      created → queued → processed → merged (Refinery handles)
```

Once a polecat's branch is pushed (cleanup_status=clean), the polecat can be
nuked immediately. The MR continues independently in the Refinery. If conflicts
arise, Refinery creates a NEW conflict-resolution task for a NEW polecat.

**Key principle**: Polecat lifecycle is separate from MR lifecycle.

## Design Philosophy

This patrol follows Gas Town principles:
- **Discovery over tracking**: Observe reality each cycle, don't maintain state
- **Events over state**: POLECAT_DONE mail triggers immediate cleanup
- **Ephemeral by default**: Clean polecats are nuked immediately, no waiting
- **Cleanup wisps for exceptions**: Only created when intervention needed
- **Task tool for parallelism**: Subagents inspect polecats, not molecule arms

## Patrol Shape (Linear, Deacon-style)

```
inbox-check ─► process-cleanups ─► check-refinery ─► survey-workers
                                                            │
         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         ▼
  check-timer-gates ─► check-swarm ─► ping-deacon ─► patrol-cleanup ─► context-check ─► loop-or-exit
```

No dynamic arms. No fanout gates. No persistent nudge counters.
State is discovered each cycle from reality (tmux, beads, mail).
